mainTopic: Why the גבעונים (נתינים) are kept out of the Jewish people: the end of דוד's search for the cause of the famine, his attempt to appease the גבעונים, his statement about the three signs of the Jewish nation, and how the seven sons of שאול were chosen.
overview: This amud finishes the story of the famine in דוד's days. It is too late to eulogize שאול, so דוד tries to make peace with the גבעונים, whom שאול had wronged. They refuse every offer and demand seven of שאול's sons. Seeing their cruelty, דוד says the Jewish people are marked by mercy, bashfulness and kindness, and only someone with these traits may join them. רב הונא explains that the ארון picked the seven sons. The גמרא then works out how דוד could spare מפיבשת without showing משוא פנים. Next it asks how the תורה's rules could be set aside: children killed for a father's sin, and bodies left hanging unburied. It answers that this prevented a חילול השם and brought a great קידוש השם, which led 150,000 converts to join. Finally the גמרא explains that משה, יהושע and דוד each decreed against the נתינים, and דוד's decree reached the furthest.

steps.title: Too late to eulogize שאול
steps.stepSummary: דוד finishes his thought: the twelve-month mourning period for שאול has passed, so a eulogy now would not be fitting.
steps.simpleTranslation: The twelve months of the year of mourning have already passed, and it is not the proper way to eulogize him now.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes דוד's reasoning about the famine. He decides that the first possible fix, eulogizing שאול properly, can no longer be done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דוד had found two wrongs from שאול's time that could explain the famine. Because a eulogy belongs within the year of mourning, he sets this one aside. That leaves only the problem of the גבעונים, which the next step takes up.

phrases.english: The twelve months of the year [of mourning have passed],
phrases.notes: This picks up in the middle of דוד's sentence about שאול. The start of the sentence comes just before this section.

phrases.english: and it is not the proper way to eulogize him [now].

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּרֵיסַר יַרְחֵי שַׁתָּא, וְלָא דַּרְכֵּיהּ לְמִסְפְּדֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes דוד's reasoning, which began before this section, about the wrong done to שאול.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A eulogy is not given once the twelve months of mourning have passed, so דוד cannot fix this wrong.

steps.title: דוד tries to appease the גבעונים
steps.stepSummary: דוד decides to appease the גבעונים. The פסוק shows his offer and their demand for seven of שאול's sons, and he cannot win them over.
steps.simpleTranslation: As for the גבעונים, let us call them and appease them. As the פסוק says: "The king called the גבעונים and said to them: What shall I do for you, and how shall I make atonement, so that you will bless the inheritance of ה'? The גבעונים said: We have no claim of silver or gold against שאול or his house, and it is not for us to kill any man... Let seven of his sons be given to us, and we will hang them up to ה'." He tried to appease them, but they would not be appeased.
steps.whatsHappening: דוד turns to the second wrong and tries to make peace with the גבעונים. They refuse everything except the death of seven of שאול's sons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא brings the פסוקים from שמואל ב to show that דוד really did try to make things right. The words "he tried to appease them, but they would not be appeased" are the key point. Their refusal to forgive sets up דוד's harsh judgment of them in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The גבעונים, who were assigned to serve as woodchoppers and water-drawers
And we will hang them up

steps.whyThisMatters: Their refusal to be appeased is the reason, in the steps that follow, that the גבעונים are judged unfit to join the Jewish people.

phrases.english: The Gibeonites: let us call them and appease them.
"And the king called the Gibeonites
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 21:2–6

phrases.english: and said to them.
What shall I do for you,
and with what shall I make atonement,
so that you may bless the inheritance of the Lord?
And the Gibeonites said to him:
We have no [claim of] silver or gold
against Saul or against his house,
nor is it for us [to kill] any man, etc.
Let seven men of his sons be given to us
and we will hang them up to the Lord, etc."
He tried to appease them, but they would not be appeased.

steps.triggerLanguage: נְתִינִים נִיקְרִינְהוּ וּנְפַיְּיסִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: With the eulogy ruled out, דוד turns to the remaining wrong: the גבעונים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד tried to appease the גבעונים, but they refused to forgive and demanded seven of שאול's sons.

steps.title: The three signs of the Jewish nation
steps.stepSummary: דוד declares that the Jewish people have three signs: they are merciful, bashful, and kind.
steps.simpleTranslation: דוד said: This nation has three distinguishing signs. They are merciful, they are bashful, and they do acts of kindness.
steps.whatsHappening: Reacting to the cruelty of the גבעונים, דוד names three traits that mark a true member of the Jewish people. The next steps give a פסוק for each trait and then draw the conclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גבעונים refused to show mercy, so דוד uses them as a contrast. He describes what the Jewish nation is really like. This list becomes the test for who may join the nation.

keyTerms.meaning: Bashful people, who have a sense of shame
People who do acts of kindness

phrases.english: He said: Three distinguishing signs
phrases.notes: "He" is דוד, reacting to how harsh the גבעונים were.

phrases.english: are found in this nation:
they are merciful, bashful, and do acts of kindness.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר, שְׁלֹשָׁה סִימָנִים יֵשׁ בְּאוּמָּה זוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: דוד responds to the refusal of the גבעונים by describing the true traits of the Jewish people.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Jewish people are marked by three traits: mercy, bashfulness, and kindness.

steps.title: A פסוק for each of the three signs
steps.stepSummary: Each of the three traits is backed up by a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Merciful, as it says: "He will give you mercy, have mercy on you, and multiply you." Bashful, as it says: "So that His fear will be on your faces." Kind, as it says: "So that he will command his children and his household..."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a separate פסוק to prove each of the three traits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first פסוק, ה' gives mercy to us, so mercy becomes part of who we are. In the second, fear "on your faces" means a sense of shame that shows on the face. In the third, אברהם teaches his household the way of ה', and the rest of that פסוק speaks of doing צדקה, which is kindness.

keyTerms.meaning: His fear upon your faces, meaning shame that shows on the face

phrases.english: Merciful, as it is written:
"And He will give you mercy, and have mercy on you, and multiply you."
phrases.notes: דברים 13:18

phrases.english: Bashful, as it is written:
"So that His fear will be upon your faces."
phrases.notes: שמות 20:17. Fear that shows on the face is a sense of shame.

phrases.english: Doing acts of kindness, as it is written:
"So that he will command his children
and his household, etc."
phrases.notes: בראשית 18:19. The "etc." points to the rest of the פסוק, which speaks of doing צדקה and justice.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַחְמָנִים — דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source from the פסוקים for each trait listed in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: The three traits of the Jewish nation: mercy, bashfulness, and kindness.

steps.title: Only someone with these traits may join the nation
steps.stepSummary: Whoever has all three signs is fit to join the Jewish people.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whoever has these three signs is fit to cling to this nation.
steps.whatsHappening: דוד draws the conclusion from the three signs: they decide who is fit to join the Jewish people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the גבעונים showed no mercy, they fail this test. This is the background for why the נתינים are kept from marrying into the Jewish people, which is the topic of our מסכת.
steps.whatToRemember: דוד's rule is that mercy, bashfulness, and kindness are the signs of the Jewish people, and only someone with them is fit to join. The cruel גבעונים fail this test.

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ שְׁלֹשָׁה סִימָנִים הַלָּלוּ —
phrases.english: Whoever has these three signs
is fit to cling to this nation.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ שְׁלֹשָׁה סִימָנִים הַלָּלוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the practical conclusion from the three proven traits.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The three traits are the test for joining the Jewish people, so the cruel גבעונים are not fit to join.

steps.title: Why were these seven sons chosen?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק listing the seven descendants of שאול who were handed over, and asks what made these particular ones different.
steps.simpleTranslation: "The king took the two sons of רצפה daughter of איה, whom she bore to שאול, ארמוני and מפיבשת, and the five sons of מיכל daughter of שאול, whom she bore to עדריאל son of ברזילי the מחולתי." What is special about these?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the פסוק naming the seven who were handed over. Then it asks why these seven were picked out of all of שאול's descendants, setting up רב הונא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שאול had many descendants, and the פסוק does not explain why דוד chose these seven. The question is how דוד decided fairly who would be given over. The next step answers it.

phrases.english: "And the king took the two sons of
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 21:8

phrases.english: Rizpah daughter of Aiah,
whom she bore to Saul,
Armoni and Mephibosheth,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶת חֲמֵשֶׁת בְּנֵי מִיכַל בַּת שָׁאוּל
phrases.english: and the five sons of Michal daughter of Saul,
whom she bore to Adriel
son of Barzillai the Meholathite."
What is different about these?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא הָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the story of the גבעונים' demand and asks how the seven sons were selected.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why these seven descendants of שאול were chosen over all the others.

steps.title: The ארון chose them
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא explains that all of שאול's descendants were passed in front of the ארון. Those the ארון held back were handed over for death, and the rest were spared.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: They passed them in front of the ארון. Whoever the ארון held back was for death, and whoever the ארון did not hold back was for life.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the question: the choice was not made by דוד on his own but by a sign from the ארון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the ארון itself picked who would die, the choice came from Heaven and was not a human decision. This explains why these seven were taken and not any of the others.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
They passed them in front of the Ark.
Whoever the Ark held back was for death;
whoever the Ark did not hold back was for life.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: הֶעֱבִירוּם לִפְנֵי אָרוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The seven were chosen by the ארון: those it held back were handed over for death, and the others were spared.

steps.title: The king had pity on מפיבשת
steps.stepSummary: רב חנא בר קטינא quotes a פסוק saying דוד had pity on מפיבשת, which seems to clash with the idea that the ארון alone decided who would die.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנא בר קטינא challenged: the פסוק says "The king had pity on מפיבשת son of יהונתן son of שאול."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a challenge to רב הונא's explanation. If the ארון picked who would die, what did דוד's pity have to do with it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא said the ארון chose the victims. But the פסוק says דוד chose to spare מפיבשת. So how could a person's pity change a decision the ארון made?

keyTerms.meaning: raises an objection, usually from a source
מפיבשת, the son of יהונתן and grandson of שאול

phrases.english: Rav Chana bar Ketina raised an objection:
"And the king had pity
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 21:7

phrases.aramaic: עַל מְפִבֹשֶׁת בֶּן יְהוֹנָתָן בֶּן שָׁאוּל״
phrases.english: on Mephibosheth son of Jonathan son of Saul"

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵתִיב רַב חָנָא בַּר קַטִּינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's claim that the ארון alone decided
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's explanation that the ארון chose who would die
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק shows דוד's pity decided מפיבשת's fate, not the ארון

steps.title: דוד did not pass מפיבשת before the ארון
steps.stepSummary: First answer: דוד's pity meant he never brought מפיבשת in front of the ארון at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means that he did not pass him in front of the ארון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a first answer: דוד showed pity by leaving מפיבשת out of the test.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This keeps רב הונא's idea that the ארון decided. דוד simply made sure מפיבשת never faced the ארון, so he could not be picked.

keyTerms.meaning: he passed him (in front of the ארון)

phrases.english: — that he did not pass him [before the Ark].

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁלֹּא הֶעֱבִירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the פסוק
steps.terutzMaskana: דוד's pity meant he kept מפיבשת away from the ארון

steps.title: Can favoritism be shown here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: is it allowed to play favorites in a life-and-death matter left to Heaven?
steps.simpleTranslation: But is favoritism allowed in such a matter?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the first answer. It would be unfair for דוד to protect his friend's son from a test everyone else had to face.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the choice was given to Heaven through the ארון, everyone should face it equally. Leaving out מפיבשת is משוא פנים, favoring one person.

keyTerms.meaning: but is it so? (a surprised question)

phrases.english: But is there favoritism
in this matter?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מַשּׂוֹא פָּנִים יֵשׁ בַּדָּבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer in step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that דוד did not pass מפיבשת before the ארון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Skipping him would be unfair favoritism

steps.title: The ארון held him, then released him after prayer
steps.stepSummary: Second answer: מפיבשת was passed before the ארון and held back, but דוד prayed and the ארון let him go.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: he passed him, the ארון held him back, דוד asked for mercy for him, and the ארון released him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a new answer. מפיבשת did face the ארון like everyone else, but דוד's prayer got him freed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fixes the fairness problem of step 10, since מפיבשת was not skipped. דוד's pity now shows up as prayer after he was already chosen.

phrases.english: Rather: he passed him and [the Ark] held him back,
and he asked for mercy on him, and [the Ark] released him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא שֶׁהֶעֱבִירוֹ וּקְלָטוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of step 9
steps.terutzMaskana: מפיבשת was chosen but freed through דוד's prayer

steps.title: Still favoritism
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that this is still favoritism.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is still favoritism, isn't it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the second answer has the same problem. Freeing someone the ארון already chose is still special treatment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the ארון picked מפיבשת, freeing him means someone else must die in his place. That is still unfair to the others.

phrases.english: And still: is there favoritism in this matter?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַכַּתִּי מַשּׂוֹא פָּנִים יֵשׁ בַּדָּבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer in step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the ארון released מפיבשת after prayer
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Undoing the ארון's choice is still favoritism

steps.title: דוד prayed beforehand that the ארון not pick him
steps.stepSummary: Final answer: דוד only prayed in advance that the ארון would not choose מפיבשת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he prayed that the ארון should not hold him back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final answer. מפיבשת faced the ארון like everyone, and דוד only prayed before the test that he would not be chosen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This avoids both problems. מפיבשת was not skipped and no decision was undone. Praying beforehand is not favoritism, because Heaven still makes the choice.
steps.whatToRemember: דוד's pity for מפיבשת was only a prayer before the test. He never skipped him or undid the ארון's choice, because that would be משוא פנים.

phrases.english: Rather, he asked for mercy
that the Ark should not hold him back.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא שֶׁבִּקֵּשׁ רַחֲמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of step 11
steps.terutzMaskana: דוד prayed only before the test

steps.title: Fathers and sons are not killed for each other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how שאול's descendants could be killed when the תורה says children are not put to death for a parent's sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written: "Fathers shall not be put to death for children" and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks a new question about the whole story. The תורה forbids killing children for what a father did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שאול's descendants did not commit the sin themselves. Handing them over seems to go directly against a פסוק in the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: but isn't it written (a challenge from a פסוק)
fathers shall not be killed for children

phrases.english: But isn't it written:
"Fathers shall not be put to death for children, etc."?
phrases.notes: דברים 24:16. The part that matters here is the rest of the פסוק: children shall not die for fathers.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא כְּתִיב לֹא יוּמְתוּ אָבוֹת עַל בָּנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about the story itself
steps.kashyaTarget: The handing over of שאול's descendants
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תורה forbids killing children for a parent's sin

steps.title: Better to uproot a letter than to cause public חילול השם
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that it is better to set aside one part of the תורה than to let Heaven's name be shamed in public.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: It is better that one letter be uprooted from the תורה than that Heaven's name be shamed in public.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. In this special case, preventing public shame to ה׳'s name was more important than this one rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן admits the rule was set aside here. He explains that a public חילול השם is so serious that it can outweigh one law of the תורה in a case like this.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how seriously the גמרא treats public חילול השם, enough to explain an exception to a clear rule.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said
Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: מוּטָב שֶׁתֵּעָקֵר אוֹת אַחַת מִן הַתּוֹרָה,
phrases.english: Better that one letter be uprooted from the Torah,
phrases.notes: "One letter" means one small part of the תורה, here the rule from the פסוק just quoted.

phrases.english: and let the Name of Heaven not be desecrated in public.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מוּטָב שֶׁתֵּעָקֵר אוֹת אַחַת מִן הַתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14
steps.terutzResolutionType: Exception based on a greater value
steps.terutzMaskana: Preventing public חילול השם justified setting aside the rule

steps.title: רצפה guards the bodies from harvest until the rain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק describing רצפה guarding the hanged bodies for a long time.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And רצפה daughter of איה took sackcloth and spread it on the rock, from the start of harvest until rain fell on them, and did not let birds rest on them by day or animals by night."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a פסוק to set up its next question. It shows the bodies stayed hanging for many weeks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key detail is the time: from the start of harvest until the rains. That means the bodies were not buried for a long time, which leads to the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: רצפה, mother of two of the seven

phrases.english: "And Rizpah daughter of Aiah took the sackcloth
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 21:10

phrases.english: and spread it for herself on the rock

steps.title: A body may not stay overnight on the tree
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the bodies could stay unburied when the תורה says a hanged body may not remain overnight.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written: "His body shall not stay overnight on the tree"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question on the פסוק it just quoted. The next step answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה requires burying a hanged person the same day. Yet these bodies stayed up for weeks, which seems to break that rule.

keyTerms.meaning: tree, the post used for hanging

phrases.english: But isn't it written:
"His body shall not remain overnight on the tree"!
phrases.notes: דברים 21:23

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא כְּתִיב לֹא תָלִין נִבְלָתוֹ עַל הָעֵץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the event described in step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: Leaving the bodies unburied for weeks
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תורה requires burial before nightfall

steps.title: Leaving the bodies up caused a great public sanctification of Heaven's name
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק, explains that it is worth setting aside one letter of the תורה so that Heaven's name is sanctified in public. The hanging bodies made people see how seriously the Jewish people protect converts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק: It is better that one letter be uprooted from the תורה, so that Heaven's name is sanctified in public. Passersby would ask, 'What did these people do?' They were told, 'These are sons of kings, and they harmed converts who joined for personal gain.' The passersby said, 'There is no nation as worthy to join as this one. If sons of kings are punished like this, ordinary people certainly would be. If even insincere converts are protected like this, born Jews certainly would be.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 17 (how could the bodies stay up overnight?). It explains that the long public display brought about a huge קידוש השם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of לא תלין is set aside here for a greater goal: making Heaven's name holy in front of the whole world. The passersby reason with a קל וחומר: if princes were punished for harming insincere converts, then surely ordinary people, and surely born Jews, are protected too.

keyTerms.meaning: That one letter (one small part of the תורה) be uprooted
In public, out in the open
Converts who joined for personal gain, not sincerely (here: the גבעונים)
How much more so (the language of a קל וחומר)

steps.confusionAlert: This sounds like step 15, but it is a different point. Step 15 was about avoiding a public shaming of Heaven's name (killing the children). This step is about actively sanctifying Heaven's name (leaving the bodies up).
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key principle: a public קידוש השם can justify setting aside a specific rule of the תורה in an unusual situation.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוֹצָדָק:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yehotzadak:

phrases.aramaic: מוּטָב שֶׁתֵּעָקֵר אוֹת אַחַת מִן הַתּוֹרָה,
phrases.english: It is better that one letter be uprooted from the Torah,
phrases.notes: The 'letter' here is the rule against leaving a hanged body up overnight.

phrases.english: and the name of Heaven be sanctified in public.
For the people passing back and forth would say:
What is the story of these people?
These are sons of kings.
And what did they do?
They raised their hands against converts who joined for gain.
phrases.notes: These are the גבעונים, who joined the Jewish people by trickery and for their own benefit.

phrases.english: They said: There is no nation
as worthy to attach oneself to as this one.
If sons of kings are treated like this,

phrases.aramaic: בְּנֵי הֶדְיוֹטוֹת עַל אַחַת כַּמָּה וְכַמָּה!
phrases.english: how much more so sons of ordinary people!
And if converts who joined for gain are treated like this,
how much more so born Jews!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוֹצָדָק: מוּטָב שֶׁתֵּעָקֵר אוֹת אַחַת מִן הַתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 17 about leaving the bodies unburied overnight.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A higher value (קידוש השם) overrides a specific prohibition in this situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Leaving the bodies hanging seems to clearly violate לא תלין נבלתו.
steps.terutzMaskana: Setting aside the rule was justified because it brought a great public קידוש השם.

steps.title: 150,000 people converted as a result
steps.stepSummary: Right away, 150,000 converts joined the Jewish people. The גמרא supports this with a פסוק about שלמה's 70,000 carriers and 80,000 stonecutters.
steps.simpleTranslation: Immediately, 150,000 people joined the Jewish people, as it says: 'And שלמה had 70,000 who carried loads and 80,000 who cut stone in the mountains.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא describes the result of the קידוש השם, a huge number of converts, and brings a פסוק as its source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא adds 70,000 and 80,000 to reach 150,000. It assumes these workers in שלמה's time were the converts. The next steps will test that assumption.

phrases.english: Immediately there were added to the Jewish people
one hundred and fifty thousand,
as it is stated: 'And Shlomo had
phrases.notes: מלכים א 5:29

phrases.english: seventy thousand who carried loads
and eighty thousand who cut stone in the mountain.'
phrases.notes: 70,000 plus 80,000 equals the 150,000 converts.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיָּד נִתּוֹסְפוּ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל מֵאָה וַחֲמִשִּׁים אֶלֶף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Describes the outcome of the קידוש השם from step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The public קידוש השם led 150,000 people to convert, as shown by שלמה's workers.

steps.title: Maybe those workers were born Jews
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the proof: perhaps שלמה's carriers and stonecutters were ordinary Jews, not converts.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe they were Jews?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pokes a hole in the proof from step 19. The פסוק never says the workers were converts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof only works if the 150,000 workers were converts. If they were born Jews, the פסוק proves nothing about converts.

phrases.english: But perhaps they were Jews?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא יִשְׂרָאֵל הֲווֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof brought in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that שלמה's 150,000 workers were converts
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק does not say they were converts, so they could have been born Jews.

steps.title: שלמה did not make Jews into slaves
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea, since a פסוק says שלמה did not make any Jews into slaves. So the laborers could not have been born Jews.
steps.simpleTranslation: You cannot think that, because it is written: 'But of the children of ישראל, שלמה made no slaves.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends its proof with another פסוק showing that born Jews were not used for this kind of slave labor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying loads and cutting stone is treated as slave work. Since שלמה made no Jew a slave, these workers must have been converts.

keyTerms.meaning: It cannot enter your mind (that idea is impossible)

phrases.english: This cannot enter your mind,
as it is written: 'But of the children of Israel
phrases.notes: מלכים א 9:22

phrases.english: Shlomo made no slave.'

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ, דִּכְתִיב: ״וּמִבְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא נָתַן שְׁלֹמֹה עָבֶד״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a second פסוק that rules out the alternative
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The workers could have been born Jews.
steps.terutzMaskana: Jews were not made into slaves, so the workers were converts.

steps.title: Maybe they were just public workers, not slaves
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: perhaps these men were simply drafted into public service, not slaves. In that case they could still have been born Jews.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps they were just workers drafted for public service.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the defense from step 21. The 'no slaves' פסוק does not rule out Jews who worked for the king without being slaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The defense depended on the workers being slaves. If they were only conscripted laborers, the פסוק about slaves no longer applies, and the proof falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: A worker drafted into the king's service (not a slave)

phrases.english: But perhaps they were merely drafted workers.
phrases.notes: Drafted workers serve the king but are free people, so they could be born Jews.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא דּוּגְזַר בְּעָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from מלכים, even with the defense of step 21.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from מלכים א 5:29
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Load carriers and stonecutters may have been free conscripts rather than slaves, so they might have been born Jews.

steps.title: A better proof: שלמה counted the converts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a פסוק from דברי הימים that says outright that שלמה counted the converts, found 150,000, and made them into carriers and stonecutters.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the proof is from here: 'And שלמה counted all the converted men in ארץ ישראל, and they were found to be 150,000, and he made 70,000 of them carriers and 80,000 stonecutters in the mountains.'
steps.whatsHappening: Since the first proof was rejected, the גמרא replaces it with a clearer פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This פסוק says clearly that the 150,000 were converts (גרים), so the question of whether they were Jews or slaves disappears. This confirms the claim of step 19.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, the proof is from here

steps.whatToRemember: The public קידוש השם caused 150,000 converts to join, and this is proven from דברי הימים ב 2:16–17, which calls them converts outright.

phrases.english: Rather, it is from here:
'And Shlomo counted all the converted men
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב 2:16–17

phrases.english: who were in the Land of Israel, etc.
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets, וגו׳, means 'and so on.' The גמרא skips part of the פסוק.

phrases.english: and they were found to be one hundred and fifty thousand, etc.
and he made seventy thousand of them carriers of loads
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets, since the פסוק in דברי הימים just says סבל.

phrases.english: and eighty thousand stonecutters in the mountain.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵהָכָא: ״וַיִּסְפֹּר שְׁלֹמֹה כׇּל הָאֲנָשִׁים הַגֵּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the proof that was rejected in step 22.
steps.raayaObject: That 150,000 converts joined in that era
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברי הימים ב 2:16–17, which explicitly calls the 150,000 workers converts

steps.title: Didn't משה already make the decree against the נתינים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the main topic and asks how דוד could have decreed against the נתינים when משה had already done so.
steps.simpleTranslation: And was it דוד who made the decree against the נתינים? It was משה who decreed against them, as it is written: 'from the one who chops your wood to the one who draws your water.'
steps.whatsHappening: The side discussion about the converts is over. The גמרא now returns to its earlier claim that דוד decreed against the נתינים, and challenges it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in משה's time already mentions a separate class of wood choppers and water drawers. That suggests משה, not דוד, set the נתינים apart.

keyTerms.meaning: The גבעונים, who were set apart as a separate group, not allowed to marry into the Jewish people
The one who chops your wood
The one who draws your water

phrases.english: And the Netinim, did David make the decree against them?
Moshe made the decree against them,
as it is written: 'From the one who chops your wood
phrases.notes: דברים 29:10

phrases.english: to the one who draws your water'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּנְתִינִים דָּוִד גָּזַר עֲלֵיהֶם? מֹשֶׁה גָּזַר עֲלֵיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side point about converts and returns to the earlier claim about דוד's decree.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that דוד made the decree against the נתינים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק from משה's time already shows the wood choppers and water drawers as a separate class, so the decree seems to come from משה.

steps.title: משה's decree was for one generation; דוד's was for all generations
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that משה's decree applied only to his own generation, and דוד extended it to all future generations.
steps.simpleTranslation: משה decreed for that generation; דוד decreed for all generations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge by showing that both decrees happened, but each had a different reach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both claims are true. משה separated the נתינים only for his time. דוד made the separation permanent, so the permanent ban comes from דוד.
steps.whatToRemember: The ban on marrying נתינים started with משה for one generation, and דוד made it permanent for all generations.

phrases.english: Moshe decreed for that generation,
David decreed for all generations.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֹשֶׁה גְּזַר לְהָהוּא דָּרָא, דָּוִד גְּזַר לְכוּלֵּי דָּרֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the two decrees by how long each one lasts
steps.terutzHavaAmina: משה's decree seems to make דוד's decree unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: משה's decree was temporary, for one generation; דוד made it permanent for all generations.

steps.title: יהושע already decreed against the גבעונים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why דוד needed a decree, since יהושע already made the גבעונים servants for all time.
steps.simpleTranslation: But still, יהושע decreed against them, as it is written: 'And יהושע made them that day hewers of wood and drawers of water for the congregation and for the altar of ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge against the answer from step 25. Even if משה's decree was only for his own generation, יהושע decreed against the נתינים after him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 25 said דוד extended the decree to all generations. But the פסוק in יהושע says יהושע made the גבעונים servants, and that seems to be a lasting arrangement. If so, דוד's decree still looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: But still. It opens a further difficulty that remains.
יהושע, the leader of the Jewish people after משה

phrases.english: But still, יהושע decreed against them,
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the גבעונים, who became the נתינים.

phrases.english: as it is written:
'And יהושע made them that day
phrases.notes: יהושע 9:27

phrases.english: hewers of wood and drawers of water
for the congregation and for the altar of ה׳'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַכַּתִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ גְּזַר עֲלַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 25 by pointing to a decree made after משה's generation.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that דוד was the first to extend the decree beyond משה's generation
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק shows that יהושע, after משה, already made the גבעונים permanent servants, so דוד's decree seems redundant.

steps.title: יהושע's decree was for the time of the בית המקדש, דוד's for all times
steps.stepSummary: יהושע's decree applied only while the בית המקדש stood. דוד extended it to times when the בית המקדש is not standing.
steps.simpleTranslation: יהושע decreed for the time when the בית המקדש is standing. דוד decreed for the time when the בית המקדש is not standing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Each decree covered a different time period, so דוד added something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'for the altar of ה׳' show that יהושע's decree was tied to serving the altar, so it applied only while the בית המקדש stood. דוד's decree went further and covers times with no בית המקדש. That gives דוד's decree its own purpose.
steps.whatToRemember: The decree against the נתינים grew in three stages. משה's decree covered his own generation. יהושע's covered the times when the בית המקדש stands. דוד's covers all times, even when there is no בית המקדש.

phrases.english: יהושע decreed
for the time when the Temple is standing,
phrases.notes: This comes from 'for the altar of ה׳' in the פסוק. An altar means a working Temple.

phrases.english: David decreed
for the time when the Temple is not standing.

steps.triggerLanguage: יְהוֹשֻׁעַ גָּזַר בִּזְמַן שֶׁבֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ קַיָּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 26 by limiting the time period of יהושע's decree.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the earlier decree to a particular time period
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יהושע's decree was permanent in every situation, which would make דוד's decree unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: יהושע's decree was tied to the altar, so it applied only when the בית המקדש stands. דוד extended it to when it does not stand.
